{{short description|Type of generating function in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], an '''Igusa zeta function''' is a type of [[generating function]], counting the number of solutions of an equation, ''modulo'' ''p'', ''p''<sup>2</sup>, ''p''<sup>3</sup>, and so on.

== Definition ==

For a [[prime number]] ''p'' let ''K'' be a [[p-adic field]], i.e. <math> [K: \mathbb{Q}_p]<\infty </math>, ''R'' the [[valuation ring]] and ''P'' the maximal [[Ideal (ring theory)|ideal]]. For <math>z \in K</math> we denote by <math>\operatorname{ord}(z)</math>  the [[Valuation (algebra)|valuation]] of ''z'', <math>\mid z \mid = q^{-\operatorname{ord}(z)}</math>, and <math>ac(z)=z \pi^{-\operatorname{ord}(z)}</math> for a uniformizing parameter &pi; of ''R''.

Furthermore let <math>\phi : K^n \to \mathbb{C}</math> be a [[Schwartz–Bruhat function]], i.e. a locally constant function with [[compact support]] and let <math>\chi</math> be a [[Character (mathematics)|character]] of <math>R^\times</math>.

In this situation one associates to a non-constant [[polynomial]] <math>f(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \in K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]</math> the Igusa zeta function

: <math> Z_\phi(s,\chi) = \int_{K^n} \phi(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \chi(ac(f(x_1,\ldots,x_n))) |f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)|^s \, dx </math>

where <math>s \in \mathbb{C}, \operatorname{Re}(s)>0,</math> and ''dx'' is [[Haar measure]] so normalized that <math>R^n</math> has measure 1.

== Igusa's theorem ==
{{harvs|txt|authorlink=Jun-Ichi Igusa|first=Jun-Ichi|last=Igusa|year=1974}} showed that <math>Z_\phi (s,\chi)</math> is a rational function in <math>t=q^{-s}</math>. The proof uses [[Heisuke Hironaka]]'s theorem about the [[resolution of singularities]]. Later, an entirely different proof was given by [[Jan Denef]] using p-adic cell decomposition. Little is known, however, about explicit formulas. (There are some results about Igusa zeta functions of [[Fermat varieties]].)

== Congruences modulo powers of ''P'' ==
Henceforth we take <math>\phi</math> to be the [[Indicator function|characteristic function]] of <math>R^n</math> and <math>\chi</math> to be the trivial character. Let <math>N_i</math> denote the number of solutions of the [[congruence relation|congruence]]

:<math>f(x_1,\ldots,x_n) \equiv 0 \mod P^i</math>.

Then the Igusa zeta function

: <math>Z(t)= \int_{R^n} |f(x_1,\ldots,x_n)|^t \, dx </math>

is closely related to the Poincaré series

: <math>P(t)= \sum_{i=0}^{\infty} q^{-in}N_i t^i</math>

by

: <math>P(t)= \frac{1-t Z(t)}{1-t}.</math>
